extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-step process using a noisy classifier to find relevant passages for workers to generate questions, followed by a model predicting answer distractors to aid workers in creating multiple choice questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks from online learning resources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter model classified individual sentences and accepted paragraphs if a minimum number of sentences was accepted, filtering out undesirable sentences based on lexical, grammatical, pragmatical, and complexity rules.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers judged whether the question could appear in a school science exam, selected up to two of six suggested distractors, and wrote at least one distractor themselves.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training data for models that answer real science questions.

name.evidence: With this method we have assembled SciQ , a dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We use a two-step process to solve these problems, first using a noisy classifier to find relevant passages and showing several options to workers to select from when generating a question. Second, we use a model trained on real science exam questions to predict good answer distractors given a question and a correct answer.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The task was advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk , requiring Master’s status for the crowdworkers, and paying a compensation of 0.30$ per HIT.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We chose science study textbooks as our base corpus because they are directly relevant and linguistically tailored towards a student audience.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We designed a rule-based document filter model into which individual paragraphs of the base corpus are fed. The system classifies individual sentences and accepts a paragraph if a minimum number of sentences is accepted.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The first instruction was to judge whether the question could appear in a school science exam... The second instruction was to select up to two of the six suggested distractors, and to write at least one distractor by themselves such that there is a total of three.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: The task was advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk , requiring Master’s status for the crowdworkers...

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: As classifier we chose a random forest (Breiman, 2001), because of its robust performance in small and mid-sized data settings and its power to incorporate nonlinear feature interactions

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: When using SciQ as additional training data to existing questions, we observe accuracy improvements on real science exams.
